event.name: 2 December 2002 Vartholomio, western Peloponnese, Greece, earthquake
event.tectonic_setting: Western Peloponnese; strike-slip deformation between the Ionian Cephalonia-Lefkada transform and the Hellenic subduction zone. Preferred sinistral NW-SE plane is not statistically distinguished decisively from the conjugate plane.

reference.title: A study of the 2 December 2002 (M5.5) Vartholomio (western Peloponnese, Greece) earthquake and of its largest aftershocks

inversion.method: Broadband empirical Green's-function deconvolution followed by source-time-function inversion (Mori-Hartzell/Dreger), with positivity and spatial derivative smoothing; preferred rupture velocity 2.7 km/s and rise time 0.4 s.
inversion.green_function_model: Empirical Green's functions from a nearby M4.1 event on 30 September 2002, replacing theoretical path/instrument/radiation response in the slip inversion.
inversion.notes: FIGURE 7 VISIBLE-WINDOW COLOR/GRAYSCALE DIGITIZATION, NOT ORIGINAL COEFFICIENTS. The paper states a 20 x 20 km inversion fault plane discretized into 0.5 km^2 patches, but Figure 7 exposes only local coordinates 0-8 km along strike and 0-10 km down dip. The dashed figure grid is visibly spaced at 0.5-km intervals, so this geobrowser record samples the VISIBLE 8 x 10 km image window at 16 x 20 image cells (0.5 x 0.5 km); these 320 plotted image cells MUST NOT be represented as the full original inversion mesh or as author-confirmed 0.25 km^2 patches. No values are inserted for the unshown portion of the original 20 x 20 km plane. Figure 7 grayscale legend is 0-10 cm; raster values are rounded 1-cm grayscale classes, not exact inversion coefficients. White/non-colored pixels are encoded as zero-compatible 0.0 m in this legacy schema but cannot establish exact zero slip or distinguish sub-centimeter slip, and compass/star/leader/contour labels mask a few regions. QA CSV identifies potentially obscured cells. Published slip maximum ~7 cm, whereas the image-cell sampled maximum is 5 cm; authors report slip patch about 3.5 x 5.5 km and published M0 1.89e17 N m. None of these published metrics is inferred by summing this incomplete visible-grid raster. The preferred sinistral NW-SE nodal plane, strike 315, dip 77, rake -22 deg, comes from source Table 2; it is statistically only weakly favored over the conjugate strike 50, dip 68, rake -166 solution. The top depth 11.626 km is an inferred alignment to the secondary depth axis (12.6 km absolute depth at 1 km down dip, assuming dip 77 deg), NOT an independently reported top depth of the 20 x 20 km inversion plane. Coordinates for individual cells cannot be uniquely reconstructed from this figure and are null. Source hypocenter 37.83 N 21.12 E 17 km from Table 2. Model data type other represents regional broadband waveforms because this schema has no broadband-regional category.
